1._section_summary: This section reports a single sample of 253 Portuguese women from the general population aged 18–50 (M=25.00, SD=7.15). Mean BMI was 21.76 kg/m2 (SD=3.26) with 10.67% underweight, 74.70% normal weight, and 14.63% overweight. 2._section_summary: This section describes the procedures and recruitment: participants were recruited via online advertisements on Facebook and by e-mail and completed an online survey; informed consent was obtained. After exclusions (males and participants younger than 18 or older than 50), the final sample comprised 253 female participants. 4._section_summary: This discussion summarizes a single study (N=253 women from the general population) that tested a mediated model where social safeness predicts disordered eating via body appreciation (BAS-2) and inflexible eating rules, controlling for BMI. 5._section_summary: This Discussion reports results from a single cross-sectional study (N=253) of women from the general population showing that social safeness is positively associated with body appreciation (BAS-2) and negatively associated with inflexible eating rules and disordered eating; path analysis indicated these two mechanisms mediate the association between social safeness and eating psychopathology (model explained R2 = 0.58 for EDE-Q). Limitations noted include the cross-sectional design, exclusive use of self-report measures, and an all-female general population sample, limiting causal inference and generalizability.

6._section_summary: This Discussion reports a single cross-sectional study testing a path model in a sample of women from the general population (N=253) examining social safeness, body appreciation (BAS-2), inflexible eating rules (IEQ), BMI, and disordered eating (EDE-Q).
